 Jim Cramer says to buy stock in this sleeping tech giant 'aggressively, aggressively'
 Published Thu, Nov 19 2026 12:15 PM EST Natasha Abellard Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer holds a "Morning Meeting" livestream at 10:20 a.m. ET. Here's a recap of Thursday's key moments. 1. The tech-heavy Nasdaq was higher when Morning Meeting was recorded as investors braced for the first day of trading in Anthropic’s historic initial public offering. The index has since turned lower, while Anthropic stock debuted up big. The artificial intelligence startup raised a record $81 billion, topping SpaceX’s June offering. “If you can get [Anthropic] shares below $120 [per share], it's a good deal,” Jim Cramer said before the stock opened. Just before noon ET, it was trading up 25% to around $104. “Anthropic is another one that you buy and give it to your kids.” Jim described both Anthropic and SpaceX as “really great companies" but said he prefers SpaceX . 2. Microsoft was up slightly, gaining for a second consecutive session as the Club stock continued to recover from last week's Outlook outage. "It was one of those crazy perfect storms where there was a latent bug that got sort of found only during a particular traffic pattern," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella told Jim on "Mad Money" on Wednesday evening. Beyond the outage, Nadella said that its Copilot suite is continuing to do well. Nadella also emphasized Microsoft's commitment to spending discipline, making clear that the company intends to live within its means. Jim said that such a stance means Microsoft stock is poised for big gains. "I would buy it aggressively, aggressively," he stressed. 3. Palo Alto Networks rose about 5% following Wednesday’s strong quarterly results. The Club holding beat expectations on both revenue and earnings per share and raised its full-year outlook, underscoring the growing demand for cybersecurity in the artificial intelligence era. The company also announced a $4.5 billion acquisition of AI startup Applied Compute, aimed at strengthening its AI security capabilities. Jim caught up with Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora to discuss the recent tech outages. Aurora attributed them, in part, to the inability of IT departments to keep up with new AI threats. Jim argued that these challenges reinforce the need for cybersecurity platforms like Palo Alto and fellow Club name CrowdStrike . He also praised Arora's leadership. "Nikesh is one of the most able executives in the country." As for the stock, he said, "It goes far." 4. Stocks covered in Thursday's rapid fire at the end of the video were: Walmart , Williams-Sonoma , and Bloom Energy . (Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long MSFT, CRWD, and PANW.
